title: Coordinate Plane Worksheets: Reading Ordered Pairs
intro: An ordered pair gives two positions in a fixed order: across first, then up.
html:
Across first, then up

The horizontal axis is labeled x and the vertical axis is labeled y. Their zero positions meet at the origin, (0, 0). To describe a point, read its horizontal position first and its vertical position second.

(3, 2) means three units right from zero and two units up.

The first number is the x-coordinate. The second number is the y-coordinate.

Read the point from the axes

From the marked point, follow its grid column down to the x-axis to find the first coordinate. Follow its grid row left to the y-axis to find the second. Check that both meet at the original point.

Count intervals from zero

The first grid line after zero is one unit away. Do not count the zero line as one. Each interval in these grids represents one unit.

If both coordinates are one too large: have the child start a finger on zero and count the spaces crossed, saying one only after reaching the next line.

Order changes the location

The points (3, 2) and (2, 3) are different: one is farther right, and the other is higher. Trace both on a separate grid to see why the order matters. If both coordinates are the same, as in (4, 4), explain each coordinate anyway.

Use parentheses and a comma

Write the two numbers as (3, 2). The comma separates horizontal and vertical position. This is a location, not a multiplication expression or a fraction.

Check by retracing the move

After writing an answer, return to the origin. Move right by the first coordinate and up by the second. If the path ends on the marked point, the pair matches the graph.

About this practice

Each worksheet has four distinct original coordinate diagrams. Every marked point has whole-number coordinates from 1 through 5, on a grid labeled from 0 through 5. The answer key gives the ordered pair.

This activity reads already marked points. It does not ask children to plot a new point, interpret a real-world graph, or read points on an axis with a zero coordinate. Negative coordinates are not included.
